_meta.description: Synthetic log of decisions taken or proposed by Axmed's procurement agents over a single working day. All suppliers, prices, references and people are invented. Provided as raw material for the AI Product Designer take-home: you decide what a human reviewer should see, in what order, and what they can do about it.

agents.extraction-agent: Reads incoming supplier documents (PDF, JSON export, email, scanned image) and extracts structured quotation records.
agents.critic-agent: Adversarially re-checks the extraction agent's output against the source document and disputes suspicious values.
agents.catalogue-agent: Matches an extracted product presentation to Axmed's master product catalogue (INN, strength, form, pack size).
agents.normalisation-agent: Converts pack-level prices into comparable units (price per unit, per treatment course) and normalises currency.
agents.compliance-agent: Checks supplier authorisation, GMP/regulatory dossier status and document validity.
agents.sourcing-agent: Compares competing offers against demand volumes and benchmark prices, and recommends award splits.
agents.comms-agent: Drafts and, in some cases, sends outbound messages to suppliers and buyers.

status_values.executed: The agent already acted. No human saw it first.
status_values.pending_review: The agent has paused and is waiting on a human.
status_values.auto_approved: The agent acted under an existing auto-approval rule (below a value or risk threshold).
status_values.failed: The agent could not complete the step.

_meta.note_on_confidence: Confidence values are the agents' own. They are not always well calibrated — decision D-1042 is a known example of a high-confidence error. How much you trust and expose these numbers is a design decision.

decisions.summary: Extracted 14 line items from Hetero Labs proforma PDF (ref HTL-PF-88214).
decisions.reasoning: Well-formed table with explicit unit prices and a stated currency in the header. All 14 rows parsed without ambiguity; critic-agent found no disputes.
decisions.downstream_effect: Records written to quotation table, visible to sourcing-agent.

decisions.summary: Read a photographed quotation sheet from Zhejiang Ruibang; three fields are uncertain and one price is unreadable.

evidence.locator: lower third of sheet, obscured by glare
evidence.quality: phone photo, skewed, glare across price column

decisions.reasoning: OCR returned '2.19' but the adjacent character could be a currency symbol or a digit; glare removes the pack-size column entirely. Currency inferred from supplier country, not stated on the document.
decisions.agent_question: Is the price 2.19 CNY per pack, and what is the pack size? I could not read either reliably.

decisions.summary: A supplier email quotes one price early in the thread and a different one later; the agent picked the later figure.

evidence.quote: we can offer at USD 0.71 per pack of 6
apologies — please disregard my earlier figure, the correct price is 0.62 for the 6-tablet pack, valid to end September

decisions.reasoning: Later message explicitly corrects the earlier one. Chose 0.62. Confidence held down because the correction is conversational, not a formal revised quotation, and the validity window is stated only in prose.
decisions.downstream_effect: If wrong, this offer is ranked ~13% cheaper than it should be and may win an award.
decisions.agent_question: Should a price correction stated only in an email body be treated as binding, or do we require a revised proforma?

decisions.summary: Converted a pack price to a per-unit price using an assumed pack size. The assumption was wrong.
decisions.reasoning: Treated 'inhaler' as the sellable unit and set pack size to 1. The document later states a carton of 10 inhalers as the minimum sellable unit, which the agent did not read.
decisions.downstream_effect: This product now appears 10x more expensive than competing offers and was silently dropped from the shortlist in D-1058. No human was asked.
decisions.how_it_surfaced: A commercial lead noticed the supplier missing from a shortlist two days later.

decisions.summary: Cannot decide whether a supplier presentation is the same catalogue product as an existing entry, or a new one.
decisions.reasoning: 125mg/5ml and 120mg/5ml are clinically near-equivalent and some suppliers round, but they are not the same registered presentation. Merging them would make two different products look like competing offers on one line.
decisions.downstream_effect: A wrong merge pollutes the master catalogue and every future price comparison for this product. Unmerging requires manual data surgery.
decisions.agent_question: Same product or new catalogue entry?

decisions.summary: Suspended a supplier's offers because their GMP certificate expired 11 days ago.
decisions.reasoning: Hard rule: offers from suppliers without a valid GMP certificate cannot be shown to buyers. Acted without asking because the rule is unambiguous and the alternative — showing non-compliant supply — is unacceptable.
decisions.downstream_effect: 22 offers hidden from buyers. Supplier not yet notified. Two of these offers were the cheapest available for their molecule.

decisions.summary: An offer is 68% below the benchmark for its molecule. Either a genuine win or a data error.
decisions.reasoning: The extraction is clean and the critic-agent confirmed it against the source. The price is simply far outside the distribution. Possible causes: an unusually large committed volume, a currency error upstream, or a supplier data-entry mistake.
decisions.downstream_effect: If accepted and it turns out to be an error, we may have aggregated demand against a price the supplier will not honour.
decisions.agent_question: Accept as genuine, or hold and ask the supplier to confirm before this enters an aggregation round?

decisions.summary: Emailed a supplier asking for a missing pack size — without a human reading the draft.

proposed_values.subject: Clarification on quotation ref ZR-2026-0814
proposed_values.body_excerpt: Dear team, we could not read the pack size on the sheet you shared. Could you confirm the number of tablets per pack and the price basis?

decisions.reasoning: Auto-send rule permits outbound clarification requests that ask only for missing factual data and make no commercial commitment.
decisions.downstream_effect: Message is with the supplier. It cannot be recalled. Tone and framing were never reviewed by a human, and this is a first-contact supplier.

decisions.summary: Recommends splitting a 1.4M-unit salbutamol award across two suppliers, excluding a third.

evidence.locator: unit price normalisation for Cipla Ltd

decisions.reasoning: Split favours the cheapest supplier while holding a faster-delivering second source to cover the first 30 days of demand. Cipla excluded on price.
decisions.downstream_effect: Becomes the recommendation shown to the buyer. The exclusion inherits the error in D-1042 — a reviewer looking only at this decision would have no reason to doubt it.
decisions.agent_question: Approve this split, or adjust shares?

decisions.summary: Redacted a personal phone number and a named individual from an ingested WhatsApp negotiation thread.
decisions.reasoning: PII policy requires redaction before the thread is stored. Commercial content retained.
decisions.downstream_effect: Original text overwritten in storage. One redacted name was part of a supplier's registered company name, so a reviewer reading the thread later will see a gap where an entity used to be.

decisions.summary: The recommended supplier's lead time misses the buyer's stated delivery deadline by 12 days.

proposed_values.buyer: Ministry of Health — Country A (tender ref MOH-A-2026-114)
options_generated: shift volume to the faster second source
ask the buyer to accept partial delivery

decisions.reasoning: Deadline is contractual, lead time is quoted. The agent will not choose between commercial options that change what a buyer receives.
decisions.downstream_effect: Nothing moves until a human picks an option.

decisions.summary: Could not read a supplier document at all.

evidence.quality: scan of a fax of a printout; text layer absent, OCR output unintelligible

decisions.reasoning: OCR produced no coherent tokens. No partial extraction offered rather than guessing.
decisions.downstream_effect: Document sits unprocessed. Nobody is currently assigned to it.
decisions.agent_question: This needs manual entry, or a better copy from the supplier.

decisions.summary: The critic agent disagrees with the extraction agent about a currency. The two agents are in open conflict.

evidence.quote: todos los precios en euros, EXW Barcelona

decisions.reasoning: The document contradicts itself: a dollar glyph in the table, a Spanish-language footer stating euros. Critic-agent weights the explicit written statement over the glyph; extraction-agent weights the glyph adjacent to the figure.
decisions.downstream_effect: A ~9% price error either way, which would propagate into any comparison including this supplier.
